title: Dense one-liner style hurts maintainability
evidence: soccer_data.py:281 find_matches uses chained `and`/`or` in a single unparenthesized `if` (venue/involves), and mcp_server.py:94 t_team_competitions returns a multi-clause conditional expression on one line; maintainability=0.58 in scores.json
suggestion: Split compound boolean filters and formatting comprehensions across lines and add parentheses to the venue filter for clarity

title: MCP protocol hand-rolled rather than using the official SDK
evidence: mcp_server.py:12 PROTOCOL_VERSION='2024-11-05'; handle() implements initialize/tools/list/tools/call JSON-RPC directly with no `mcp` package import
suggestion: Acceptable and dependency-free; noted for cross-run comparison since other stacks may use the SDK

title: Query surface exceeds the spec (12 tools)
evidence: mcp_server.py:127 TOOLS registers team_rankings, competition_stats, biggest_wins, derbies, team_competitions, brazilian_club_players and club_profile (cross-file FIFA+match join) beyond the required match/team/player/competition/head-to-head queries
suggestion: No action; surfaced as beyond-spec coverage

title: Venue filter relies on Python operator precedence without parentheses
evidence: soccer_data.py:281 `if venue == "home" and m.home != t or venue == "away" and m.away != t or not m.involves(t):` — correct by precedence but fragile
suggestion: Wrap each venue clause in parentheses to make the intent explicit and prevent regressions
